name: halftone-print
title: Halftone Print
description: A scene printed instead of displayed: cyan, magenta and yellow dot screens at their own angles on warm paper, each plate a touch out of register. Runs its WebGL shader over its own built-in scene (a paper poster; kicker, headline and paragraph from variables), not over the host video. Best on light, graphic scenes with real midtones.
useWhen: A scene should read as printed rather than displayed: zine intros, riso posters, editorial title cards.
The scene is light and graphic with real midtones, which is where a dot screen has something to render.
avoidWhen: Only one element should feel papery while the rest stays clean: use paper-sticker or paper-wobble.
The scene is dark: nearly every cell saturates to full ink and the screen disappears into a solid field.
Small type has to stay readable: a dot screen keeps only a cell's colour.
author: Remocn

variables.label: Kicker
variables.description: Small line above the headline in the sample poster.

variables.label: Headline
variables.default: Ship the demo, not the deck

variables.label: Body
variables.default: A recorded product beats a rehearsed one. Cut it in the afternoon and send it before the meeting.

variables.label: Dot size
variables.description: Spacing of the dot screen. Pixel sizes are for a 1280×720 frame and scale with the frame.

variables.label: Angle
variables.description: Rotation of the whole screen set.

variables.label: Misregistration
variables.description: How far the plates sit out of register. Pixel sizes are for a 1280×720 frame and scale with the frame.

variables.label: Resolution
variables.description: Share of the frame size the shader is drawn at, then scaled up. Fine dots need 1; lower renders faster but the screen turns soft.
